subject: Materials Science
title: Top-Down vs Bottom-Up Synthesis
description: One-minute skill: Top-Down vs Bottom-Up Synthesis.

hook.text: Carve a nanostructure from a block, or build it atom by atom — two philosophies for creating nanomaterials.

buildup.text: Top-down methods like milling and lithography break bulk materials into nanostructures — powerful but wasteful.

discovery.text: Bottom-up methods like chemical synthesis and self-assembly build nanostructures from atoms — precise and efficient.

twist.text: Top-down struggles below 10 nm — but bottom-up struggles with placement. Neither approach is perfect alone.

climax.text: Modern chip fabs combine both — lithography defines patterns while chemical deposition builds atomically thin layers.

punchline.text: Sculpt from the top or build from the bottom — both paths reach nanoscale.

quiz.question: What is a bottom-up nanofabrication approach?
options: Building nanostructures from atomic or molecular precursors
Etching patterns into silicon wafers with light
